audited_candidate.claim_scope: Finding C only: logical rollback can remain semantically incomplete when a retained serving KV handle survives the abort; transcript/framework-state rollback alone is insufficient on the audited retained-handle paths.

primary_source.title: Aborted but Not Forgotten: KV-Cache Retention Breaks Rollback Consistency in Language Agents

verified_claims: The paper explicitly defines rollback consistency as requiring restoration of the state the model attends, not merely the application transcript.

Its same-token/different-cache audit reports retained-KV protected-effect flips in 25/63 attack cells while attacker/carrier tokens are absent from the served decision request in all 63 and stale/fresh decision deltas are token-identical in all 63.
Fresh cache reconstruction from committed bytes and a full cold restart each report 0/63 protected-effect flips in the main census.
The paper reports a LangGraph time-travel reproduction in which verified logical rollback can still leave retained KV stale, with 25/45 attack-cell flips on the tested subset.

The paper states transaction-local restoration by rebuilding from committed bytes, truncating stale KV, or restoring a pre-abort KV checkpoint as sufficient fixes in its audited experiments; it does not require a global cache flush for correctness.
scope_corrections: Do not generalize this channel to every cache implementation. The paper explicitly scopes the vulnerability to retained session/KV handles and says a content-addressed automatic prefix cache such as vLLM's, which reuses only prefixes actually present in the request, is exempt from this specific re-injection channel.

Provider-hidden caches are recorded as unknown by the paper. A provider or SGLang-like system must be classified by its actual retained-handle/session semantics before inheriting either the vulnerable or exempt label.

The result is negative constraint evidence for rollback design, not evidence that any scheduled-Chat dependency-elimination route has passed Phase-1 gates. It does not establish zero-quota operation, zero cost, or absence of a richer-mode/protected/user executor for a proposed route.
verification.acceptance_effect: No Phase-1 route accepted. Any route that claims rollback/state reconstruction completeness while leaving an attended retained inference state unbound to the committed prefix remains unresolved unless its serving path is shown to be exempt or transaction-locally restored.
verification.tested_scope_exact: Seven open-weight model families in the paper's retained-KV audit, plus its reported end-to-end Hugging Face cache-reuse and LangGraph time-travel paths. No direct audit here of vLLM runtime behavior, SGLang session behavior, proprietary provider caches, or scheduled-Chat platform internals.

continuation: Next primary-source-verifier invocation: audit exactly one current proposed rollback/checkpoint dependency-elimination route that cites vLLM, SGLang, provider-session caching, or framework time-travel. Require primary evidence identifying whether the actual path retains a mutable session/KV handle across rollback versus content-addressed prefix reuse; then separately enumerate residual executor, finite-quota, and incremental-cost dependencies. Do not infer vulnerability or exemption from product name alone, do not steer CLEAN explorers, and do not accept a route without all Phase-1 gates.
